Generic.notes: Attacks against block ciphers regardless of structure — doesn't correspond to any single slide category. Closest conceptually to APT reconnaissance tooling.

Exploits.notes: Exploitation of a known vulnerability — mapped to APT/intrusion since UNSW's Exploits class covers post-recon compromise attempts.

Fuzzers.notes: Fuzzing tools probing for unknown vulnerabilities — closest conceptual match to zero-day discovery activity.

DoS.notes: Denial of service — direct match (UNSW's DoS includes both single- and multi-source floods).

Reconnaissance.notes: Scanning/probing prior to compromise — precursor to lateral movement in the kill chain.

Analysis.notes: Port scan + spam + HTML file penetration attacks — closest match is web/phishing-adjacent activity.

Backdoor.notes: Backdoor access techniques — direct conceptual match to C2 channels.

Shellcode.notes: Small malicious code payload delivery — used as the closest stand-in for ransomware payload delivery, since UNSW predates modern ransomware-specific labeling.

Worms.notes: Self-replicating malware — weak match; included in RL engine as malware_backdoor rather than insider. Flagged as the least clean mapping in this table.

FTP-Patator.notes: Credential brute-force — mapped to insider/credential-abuse category (matches RL engine's credential_attack threat_type).

SSH-Patator.notes: Credential brute-force — same rationale as FTP-Patator.

Bot.notes: Botnet client traffic — direct match to C2.

Infiltration.notes: Multi-stage internal compromise — direct match to APT-style long-dwell intrusion.

Heartbleed.notes: CVE-2014-0160 exploitation — direct match, this is a canonical zero-day/known-CVE case.

Web Attack \ufffd Brute Force.notes: Web application attack — grouped under phishing/web-vector category.
